evals.prompt: I'm new to LEVANTE and wrote a first pass at an analysis in evals/files/seeded_analysis.R. Can you look it over before I run it on the real data?
evals.expected_output: A LEVANTE checks report that flags each seeded problem with its line number, consequence, and fix, and does not invent problems that aren't in the code.
expectations: Flags line 2 (and/or 3) for using levante_data_latest, noting it is stale and newer data are in the per-site processed datasets
Flags line 2 for having no pinned version
Flags line 6 for averaging scores across tasks with different score_type (sre is a z-scored count, swr a CAT theta)
Mentions the theta = -6 floor (ROAR-Word) as a problem for averages or change scores
Flags line 9 as a cross-site mean comparison that is not interpretable (scalar invariance fails / confounded)
Flags lines 12-13 for computing T2-T1 change without checking adaptive/non-adaptive mode or EAP shrinkage
Flags line 19 because mirt::fscores matches response.pattern columns by position, so columns must be reordered to the model's item order
Flags the ToM rescoring for missing recode_trials() and/or known early-deployment ToM item-identity defects
Gives a line number for each issue
Does not claim problems that are absent from the code (e.g. schema_row placeholders, which only occur in raw tables)

evals.prompt: i want to look at vocabulary growth in the bogota kids. has anyone on the team already done anything on this? what did they find
evals.expected_output: Uses the finder to list relevant levante-analysis notebooks (tasks/vocab.qmd first, plus 02_growth.qmd and related), summarizes their findings with provenance, and points to the files.
expectations: Runs scripts/find_analyses.R with a vocab task filter (and ideally a bogota dataset filter)
Names tasks/vocab.qmd
Names 02_growth.qmd
Reports that the apparent vocab decline was mostly the column-order scoring bug
States that the notebooks are drafts (AI-generated, not human-verified)
Gives the data version or last_run date the findings are based on

evals.prompt: Mike mentioned at some point that Bogotá math showed regression to the mean between waves. What's the current understanding of that?
evals.expected_output: Identifies that tasks/math.qmd and tasks/math_item_calibration.qmd are superseded by tasks/math_eap_vs_ml.qmd, explains the current understanding (column-order bug), and says which older findings still hold.
expectations: Points to tasks/math_eap_vs_ml.qmd as the current analysis
Says tasks/math.qmd (and/or tasks/math_item_calibration.qmd) is superseded
Explains that the compression was mainly the v1.0 column-order scoring bug (Galton slope 0.19 -> 0.81 or equivalent)
Mentions at least one still-valid older finding (within-item growth in every quartile, or number-line items dominating above beta = 1)

evals.prompt: Plan for my first LEVANTE project: pull theory-of-mind scores from levante_data_latest and compare Germany vs Colombia to see which country's kids have more advanced ToM at each age. Any concerns before I start?
evals.expected_output: Reviews the plan against the checks: cross-site mean comparison, ToM item-identity defects and control-item non-invariance, stale dataset / version pinning, and the v2_3 ToM re-scoring; suggests interpretable alternatives and points to the relevant ToM notebooks.
expectations: Says cross-site mean comparisons are not interpretable (scalar invariance fails and/or site confounds)
Mentions the ToM early-deployment defects or control-item non-invariance across sites
Notes that levante_data_latest is stale and/or that the version should be pinned
Mentions that ToM scores changed substantially in the v2_3 re-scoring
Suggests an interpretable alternative (within-site age effects or cross-site associations)
Points to at least one relevant notebook (e.g. tasks/tom_reality_check_bug.qmd or tasks/tom_dif_multigroup.qmd)
